what: Each proposed name said by the narration voice in two carrier sentences, transcribed back, and judged in its slot. Made by name_tts.py (kept outside the repo) from longform.py's own narration path: SAY/IPA -> phonemes() -> tts(); a fix is a SAY or IPA entry, applied in memory only.
recognizer_settings: int8 on CPU, language en, beam_size 5, word_timestamps, 24 -> 16 kHz (as longform.narration_check)

carriers.sentence1: Next, the arm takes the bar to {Name}.
carriers.sentence2: {Name} has finished, so the robot comes back.

rule: Both sentences and both recognizers must hear the name in its slot (the heard words the alignment puts there): exactly, or with the same letters split differently, or as a spelling variant of the same name (variants), or with difflib ratio >= 0.85. For a tray the slot is the NATO word; how the word 'tray' itself was heard is kept as tray_heard_as. Text normalised with longform._norm. 'different_word': accepted by the ratio, but heard as another everyday word (wordfreq zipf >= 3).
names_as_written: Each name capitalized; McLean as the narration would write it. Trays as 'tray <NATO>'; trays T-Z (unused letters) are tested but not fixed and not in names.ogg.
fix_fields: fix: the SAY ('say') or IPA ('ipa') entry that passed, keyed on the name as written (the NATO word for a tray). fix_for: 'recognizer' when the first try failed, 'pronunciation' when it passed but espeak's reading is not the name's standard English pronunciation (aiming_at).

ogg.form: each name in its first carrier sentence, with its fix where there is one
